records.quote: Usual stochastic order (denoted by X ⩽st Y ): X is said to be stochastically smaller than Y if for all x, F(x) ⩾ G(x). Hazard rate ordering (denoted by X ⩽hr Y ): X is smaller than Y in hazard rate ordering if hX(x) ⩾ hY(x) ... Likelihood ratio ordering (denoted by X ⩽lr Y ): X is smaller than Y in likelihood ratio ordering if g(x)/f(x) is an increasing function of x. The following implications hold among these stochastic orders: X ⩽lr Y ⇒ X ⩽hr Y ⇒ X ⩽st Y.

conclusion.direction: X ≤_lr Y ⟹ X ≤_hr Y ⟹ X ≤_st Y
